marking.rawScoreFormula: 3 times all correct answers, minus the number of incorrect MCQs.

questionCounts.reason: No fixed 2026 question count or split was verified in the official material read. Exam Q12 says the number of non-MCQs varies and cannot be disclosed. Do not hard-code a recent year's count as a 2026 official fact.

syllabusStatus.officialEvidence: Exam FAQ Q14 explicitly says CAT does not have a defined syllabus for preparation.
syllabusStatus.curriculumStatus: The topics below are inferred preparation coverage: a deliberately broad educational selection informed by legitimate CAT preparation resources and foundational books. They are not an official exhaustive CAT 2026 syllabus, a question-frequency forecast, or a promise that every listed question type will appear.

officialMock.statusAtResearch: Announced in the official FAQ; no live 2026 mock link was present in the checked home index.
officialMock.purpose: Use the released official mock to verify interface behaviour and instructions. Do not assume its questions, count, difficulty or distribution predict the examination.

examMetadata.admissionAndScoreCaution: Course completion, practice thresholds and mock scores do not guarantee percentile, rank, a shortlist or admission. Do not publish invented cutoffs. Raw marks, percentage accuracy, scaled CAT scores and percentiles are different quantities. Institute-specific selection may include additional criteria and evaluation components.

learningDesign.audience: A learner starting with school-level arithmetic and ordinary English reading, progressing toward independent CAT-style problem solving and timed decisions.
coverageBoundaries: Vocabulary, grammar and formal logic are supporting skills, not claims that standalone vocabulary, grammar or syllogism questions must appear in CAT 2026.
Modern mathematics is bounded to counting, elementary probability, sets and sequences. Calculus, advanced probability and abstract number-theory theorems are not required by this curriculum.
The open books teach mathematics, writing and study skills. They are not marketed here as CAT coaching books.
The included questions are original instructional self-checks, not a calibrated CAT mock bank.

timeBudget.beginnerBuffer: Allow additional time for unfamiliar mathematics, English reading or interrupted study. Estimates include the assigned lecture, selected reading and assignment, but not unlimited external question-bank practice.
timeBudget.deadlineContext: September 20 to November 29 is approximately ten weeks. A 19-24 hour weekly plan can accommodate the core route and substantial review, but a genuine beginner may need a longer learning horizon. Do not represent the deadline plan as a mastery guarantee.

suggestedCalendar.focus: Orientation, calculation toolkit, RC main ideas, percentages and ratios.
RC inference, tone and arguments; interest, work and motion.
Tables, charts and caselets; paragraph ordering and summaries.
Equations, inequalities, functions and sequences; maintain daily reading.
Number properties, remainders, arrangements and grouping.
Venn diagrams, tournaments, DILR selection, triangles and circles.
Coordinates, mensuration, counting, probability and sectional practice.
First full mock and review. Check the announced official mock release from November 12.
Second full mock, forensic review and targeted repairs.
Final rehearsal early in the week, light retrieval, official-instruction checks and tapering.

weeklyRoutine: Read an authorized or open text for 25-35 minutes on five days. Record the main claim, paragraph roles, one warranted inference and one tempting unsupported inference.
Complete three deliberate QA sessions and three DILR sessions weekly; review errors before increasing speed.
Reserve one session for retrieval and delayed re-solving rather than new material.
From the intermediate stage, take a short mixed sectional exercise weekly. Label learner-assembled exercises as practice simulations, not standardized mocks.

The three planned fresh full-mock attempts can use the three free mocks advertised by Cracku, subject to availability. Additional fresh mocks are optional; do not silently assume an unlimited free series.

progressWorkflow.completionRule: Watching a video is not lesson completion. Retain the assignment deliverables, assess the rubric and schedule retrieval.
progressWorkflow.masteryRule: Use at least 8/10 on the lesson rubric and a successful delayed re-solve before marking mastered-for-now. This is a learning-platform criterion, not a CAT cutoff.
mockMetrics: Raw score using the documented marking profile
Attempted and correct counts by section and question type
Time lost on abandoned questions or sets
Unattempted questions solvable during a blind review
Two specific changes to test in the next attempt
progressWorkflow.percentileHandling: Store a provider-reported percentile with provider, cohort and test identifiers. Never manufacture a CAT percentile from this platform's raw score or compare unlike mock cohorts as if they were the same examination.

learningDesign.originalAssessmentPolicy: All 38 embedded self-checks and their passages are newly authored for this curriculum. External exam questions, coaching questions, passages and solutions are not reproduced. Thirty numerical or constraint answers were checked using exact arithmetic or enumeration; eight verbal or interpretation answers were reviewed against their supplied text.

questions.prompt: Original passage: After the town library extended its weekend hours, visits rose sharply. The director called the change an educational success. Yet visitor counts do not reveal what people learned. Some visitors came to use the internet; others attended a new children's programme introduced in the same month. Longer hours may help residents, but the library should assess reading and learning outcomes before attributing all benefits to the schedule. Which is the best main idea?
choices: A. Longer opening hours always improve learning.
B. Increased visits are encouraging but do not alone establish educational benefits from longer hours.
C. Libraries should stop providing internet access.
D. The children's programme caused every additional visit.
questions.explanation: The passage welcomes possible benefits while questioning the inference from visits to learning and the attribution to one change. The other choices add absolute or unsupported claims.

questions.prompt: Original passage: In two districts, households that joined a voluntary composting pilot reported sending less waste to landfill. The project did not measure their waste before enrolment, and participation was not randomly assigned. The organizers describe the result as promising and propose a controlled follow-up. Which conclusion is supported?
choices: A. The pilot certainly caused every household to reduce waste.
B. All households would obtain the same result.
C. The reports are encouraging, but the design does not isolate the pilot's causal effect.
D. Composting cannot reduce landfill waste.
questions.explanation: The missing baseline and nonrandom participation leave alternative explanations. The passage supports cautious interest, not either certainty of effectiveness or certainty of failure.

questions.prompt: A town doubled secure bicycle parking in April. Cycling trips then increased. An official concludes that the extra parking caused the increase. Which additional fact most directly weakens that causal attribution?
